The highest common factor of 108, 72 and 5a is a. What can be the least common multiple of 108, 72 and a?
questions.solution: $\text{HCF}(108, 72) = 36$. Since $a$ divides both 108 and 72, $a$ must divide 36. If $a = 36$, then $5a = 180$, and $\text{HCF}(108, 72, 180) = 36 = a$.\nThen $\text{LCM}(108, 72, 36) = \text{LCM}(108, 72) = 216$.

questions.questionText: The LCM of two numbers is 120 and the numbers are in the ratio 3 : 8. The sum of the numbers will be:
questions.solution: Let the numbers be $3x$ and $8x$. $\text{LCM} = 24x = 120 \implies x = 5$.\nSum $= 3x + 8x = 11x = 11 \times 5 = 55$.

questions.questionText: The HCF of two numbers is 21 and their LCM is 221 times the HCF. If one of the numbers lies between 200 and 300, then the sum of the digits of the other number is:
questions.solution:
Let numbers be $21a$ and $21b$ with $\gcd(a, b) = 1$.
$L = 21ab = 221 	imes 21 \implies ab = 221 = 13 	imes 17$.
One number $= 21 	imes 13 = 273$ (lies between 200 and 300).
Other number $= 21 	imes 17 = 357$.
Sum of digits $= 3 + 5 + 7 = 15$.

questions.questionText: The LCM of two numbers x and y is 204 times their HCF. If their HCF is 12 and the difference between the number is 60, then x + y = ?
questions.solution:
$H = 12, L = 204 	imes 12 = 12ab \implies ab = 204$.
Difference $= 12(a - b) = 60 \implies a - b = 5$.
Since $ab = 204$ and $a - b = 5$, solving: $17 	imes 12 = 204$ and $17 - 12 = 5$.
$x + y = 12(a + b) = 12(17 + 12) = 12 	imes 29 = 348$.

questions.questionText: The HCF of two 2-digit number is 19 and their sum is 152. What is their difference?
questions.solution: Numbers are $19a$ and $19b$. $19(a + b) = 152 \implies a + b = 8$.\nSince both are 2-digit numbers: $a, b \in \{3, 5\}$ ($19 \times 3 = 57, 19 \times 5 = 95$).\nDifference $= 95 - 57 = 38$.

questions.questionText: The sum of two positive numbers is 240 and then HCF is 15. Find the number of pairs of number of satisfying the given condition.
questions.solution: $15(a + b) = 240 \implies a + b = 16$ with $\gcd(a, b) = 1$.\nCoprime pairs: $(1, 15), (3, 13), (5, 11), (7, 9)$.\nTotal pairs $= 4$.

questions.solution: $10a \times 10b = 1500 \implies ab = 15$ with $\gcd(a, b) = 1$.\nCoprime pairs: $(1, 15), (3, 5)$.\nNumber of pairs $= 2$.

questions.questionText: Find the least number divisible by 2, 3, 5, 6, 9 and 18, which is a perfect square.
questions.solution: $\text{LCM}(2, 3, 5, 6, 9, 18) = 90 = 2 \times 3^2 \times 5$.\nTo make it a square, multiply by $2 \times 5 = 10$: $90 \times 10 = 900$.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest perfect square number which is completely divisible by 4, 6, 9, 12 and 15?
questions.solution: $\text{LCM}(4, 6, 9, 12, 15) = 180 = 2^2 \times 3^2 \times 5$.\nTo make it a square, multiply by 5: $180 \times 5 = 900$.

Six bells commence tolling together at 7 : 59 am. They toll at intervals of 3, 6, 9, 12 and 15 seconds respectively. How many time will they toll together till 8:16 am? (excluding the toll at 7:59 am)
questions.solution: $\text{LCM}(3, 6, 9, 12, 15) = 180\text{ seconds} = 3\text{ minutes}$.\nDuration from 7:59 am to 8:16 am $= 17\text{ minutes}$.\nNumber of tolls $= \lfloor \frac{17}{3} \rfloor = 5$.

questions.questionText: A person has three iron bars whose lengths are 20, 30 and 40 meters, respectively. He wants to cut pieces of the same length from each of the three bars. What is the least number of total pieces if he cuts without any wastage?
questions.solution: Length of each piece $= \text{HCF}(20, 30, 40) = 10\text{ m}$.\nNumber of pieces $= \frac{20}{10} + \frac{30}{10} + \frac{40}{10} = 2 + 3 + 4 = 9$.

questions.questionText: The least number of square tiles required to pave the ceiling of a room, 12m 95cm long and 3m 85 cm broad, is:
questions.solution: $L = 1295\text{ cm}, B = 385\text{ cm}$.\nSide of tile $= \text{HCF}(1295, 385) = 35\text{ cm}$.\nNumber of tiles $= \frac{1295 \times 385}{35 \times 35} = 37 \times 11 = 407$.

questions.questionText: A milk vendor has 75 litres of cow milk, 45 litres of toned milk and 30 litres of full cream milk. These should be placed in different trays such that each tray contains the same quantity of milk and two kinds of milk should not be mixed in a tray. What is the least number of trays required to place all the milk?
questions.solution: Capacity of each tray $= \text{HCF}(75, 45, 30) = 15\text{ litres}$.\nTrays required $= \frac{75}{15} + \frac{45}{15} + \frac{30}{15} = 5 + 3 + 2 = 10$.

In finding the HCF of two numbers by division method, the last divisor is 17 and the quotients are 1, 11 and 2, respectively. What is sum of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
Working backwards:
Last dividend $= 17 	imes 2 = 34$.
Previous dividend $= 34 	imes 11 + 17 = 374 + 17 = 391$.
First dividend $= 391 	imes 1 + 34 = 425$.
Numbers are 425 and 391.
Sum $= 425 + 391 = 816$.

questions.solution: Multiples of 13 less than 60 other than 13: 26, 39, 52.\n$a = 26, b = 39, c = 52$.\n$\frac{a + c}{b} = \frac{26 + 52}{39} = \frac{78}{39} = 2$.
